massEmpty.sourceNote: Wikipedia cites AR57 LLC's own product page for the AR-57 PDW carbine (7.45 lb), but that page is only reachable through a 2010 archived snapshot whose catalogue is JavaScript-driven and does not render the figure in static HTML, so it is recorded as estimated rather than independently confirmed.

length.sourceNote: Wikipedia cites AR57 LLC's own product page for the AR-57 PDW carbine (30 in); see the note on massEmpty for why this is recorded as estimated rather than verified.

barrelLength.sourceNote: Wikipedia cites AR57 LLC's own product page for the AR-57 PDW carbine (16 in); see the note on massEmpty for why this is recorded as estimated rather than verified.

capacity.sourceNote: Feeds from FN P90 magazines; Wikipedia's cited AR57 LLC image gallery page states the rifle is supplied with two 50-round P90 magazines. 10-, 30- and 40-round P90 magazines also fit.

images.alt: An AR-15-pattern carbine with a horizontal magazine sheathed in a black cloth cover running above the handguard, a red-dot sight forward of a light green lower receiver, and a fixed carbine-length stock.
images.caption: An AR-57 upper mounted on a lower receiver machined by a different maker (Defense Distributed's 'Objet'), photographed by its builder as a test fit before first firing; the horizontally mounted P90 magazine is the AR-57's defining feature.
